text: New Balance Athletics, Inc. (NB), operating as New Balance, is an American multinational footwear and apparel company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, founded in 1906 as the New Balance Arch Support Company by William J. Riley, an Irish immigrant. Riley named the company after observing chickens in his yard, noting their three-pronged feet provided balance, a concept he demonstrated by placing a chicken foot on his office desk. His first product, a flexible arch support with three support points, aimed to improve shoe fit. In 1927, Riley hired Arthur Hall as a salesman, and in 1934, Hall became a business partner; the company later operated as the New Balance Athletic Shoe Company. It gained recognition among baseball and track and field athletes during the 1930s. In 1956, Hall sold the business to his daughter Eleanor and her husband Paul Kidd, who continued selling arch supports until 1960, when they introduced the "Trackster," the first running shoe available in varying widths, which became popular through YMCA programs and was adopted by college track teams including MIT, Tufts, and Boston University. Sales declined until 1972, when 28-year-old Jim Davis acquired the company, believing in the potential of leisure-time products; at the time, the company employed six people and produced 30 pairs of shoes daily via mail-order and a few U.S. retailers. The Boston area became a hub for the running boom in the 1970s, leading to rapid growth. In 1982, New Balance opened a UK factory in Workington, relocating it to Flimby in 1991. In 2001, the company purchased PF Flyers and re-launched the brand in 2003; in February 2004, it acquired Warrior Lacrosse (now Warrior Sports) from Warren, Michigan. In 2011, New Balance placed Aravon, Cobb Hill, and Dunham under its Drydock Footwear affiliate. In 2015, New Balance’s parent company, along with Berkshire Partners, bought Rockport from Adidas and combined it with Drydock Footwear under the name The Rockport Group, which included the Aravon, Cobb Hill, Dunham, and Rockport brands. In 2018, The Rockport Group filed for bankruptcy and was sold. In February 2015, New Balance entered the global soccer market through its subsidiary Warrior Sports, which had a $40-million-a-year sponsorship deal with Liverpool F.C., and later rebranded to leverage the parent brand’s global reach. The UK High Court rejected New Balance’s legal challenge to Liverpool’s UK£70 million+ kit deal with Nike, which began in January 2020, and the Manchester United deal with Adidas for £75 million annually. In 2016, New Balance opposed the Trans Pacific Partnership, criticizing it for harming domestic manufacturing, while supporting the stance of Hillary Clinton, Bernie Sanders, and Donald Trump against the agreement; Matt Lebretton, the company’s vice president of public affairs, stated that all three candidates agreed the TPP was not the right policy. After Donald Trump won the 2016 election, Lebretton expressed optimism about improved trade relations, and some media interpreted his remarks as supportive of Trump, leading to an ad hoc boycott campaign. Owner and chairman Jim Davis donated nearly $400,000 to the Trump Victory Committee in September 2016. In December 2018, Joe Preston became president, succeeding Rob DeMartini. In March 2020, the company converted some of its New England manufacturing facilities to produce face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic. In April 2021, Teddy Santis, founder of Aimé Leon Dore, was named creative director of New Balance’s premium sneaker line. New Balance manufactures shoes and apparel with a U.S. and UK manufacturing presence, producing popular models like the 990 series in Europe, unlike many competitors who manufacture exclusively outside the U.S. and Europe, resulting in higher pricing. The company differentiates its products through technical features such as blended gel inserts, heel counters, and a broader range of sizes, especially for very narrow or very wide widths. Between 1992 and 2019, the company earned approximately $69 billion in profit. In 2017, New Balance’s Flimby, England facility produced 28,000 pairs of shoes weekly, accounting for 5% of European sales. New Balance sponsors a variety of sports, including the New York Road Runners (organizer of the New York City Marathon), the NBA, major league baseball teams the New York Mets and Boston Red Sox, Team Ireland at the Rio 2016 Olympics, and global football, athletics, and individual sports teams in basketball, baseball, cricket, cycling, tennis, rugby, lacrosse, motorsports, and skateboarding. The company has launched products in collaboration with Aimé Leon Dore, NBA star Kawhi Leonard, and British designer Paul Smith. In 2025, New Balance released a limited-edition line of Japan-made cotton T-shirts in collaboration with Shohei Ohtani, celebrating craftsmanship and cultural roots. On 1 December 2025, New Balance was named on-and-off field apparel supplier for the Perth Bears, an incoming National Rugby League (Australia) club entering the league in 2027—making the Bears the first NRL club to partner with the brand. The New Balance Foundation, established in 1981, supports national and Boston-based charities focused on health, nutrition, education, and physical activity. In 2015, New Balance committed to the Science Based Targets initiative to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius and aims to achieve 100% renewable electricity in operations by 2025. In February 2024, the company launched its resale program 'Reconsidered,' allowing pre-worn shoes to be sold on its online store. In 2011, a class-action lawsuit was filed against New Balance alleging false advertising regarding toning footwear, citing a University of Wisconsin–La Crosse study funded by the American Council on Exercise. Researchers found no statistically significant improvements in exercise response or muscle activation from wearing toning shoes, concluding there is no evidence that such shoes increase calorie burn, improve muscle tone, or enhance physical activity, though they may encourage people to walk more. In August 2012, New Balance settled the false advertising claims by paying $2.3 million.
